explanation:
[EFFECT] Humidity has a non-monotonic (inverted-U-shaped) effect on predicted hourly bike demand. At very low humidity levels (near 0%), the model assigns a noticeably negative contribution, suppressing predicted rentals. The model's contribution turns mildly positive in a moderate "sweet spot" roughly between about 30% and 60% relative humidity — this is where demand is least penalised by humidity. Beyond roughly 80% humidity, the contribution drops sharply and steeply into strongly negative territory, meaning very high humidity substantially reduces predicted demand, with the worst penalty at or near 100% humidity.

[IMPORTANCE] Humidity is the 6th most important feature out of 9, with a global importance score of 0.077. It has a meaningful but secondary influence on demand — notably smaller than the top drivers (hour of day, year, temperature, weekday, and month), yet still more influential than weather situation category, wind speed, and holiday status.

[RECOMMENDATION] On high-humidity days (above ~80% relative humidity), the model predicts a significant drop in rentals, so operators could consider reducing bike availability or staffing during such conditions, while ensuring adequate supply on moderate-humidity days where demand holds up well.
